title: What the Hunt Brings In
sceneText:
Today’s line runs west of the camp, easy slope, thin woods.

The chance at big game was spent yesterday; after that stag, today the field is out for small things. Hare, pheasant, partridge, and with luck a duck or two come up from the bottoms.

This kind of hunting needs no ceremony. The men spread out and go slowly. Thierry is somewhere up the slope, and now and then he calls, and the field leans a little in one direction.

You take a few things.

When it is counted at midday the stewards put their bags together. Somebody counts yours for you.

choices.text: Sell it on the spot for coin

effects.logEntry: You sold today’s bag on the spot for coin.

choices.resultText:
The man buying game has come out from Valehold. His scales are accurate and he names his price without fuss. He counts it, gives you a figure, and you find it fair enough.

He settles on the spot. Your share goes into a basket with everyone else’s.

choices.text: Take it back to the estate

effects.logEntry: You carried today’s bag back to Maplegate.

choices.resultText:
You say you will take it back.

A steward from another house glances at you — the look that means, so there are still people who do it that way. Most of them take the coin. Carrying it home means it has to be dealt with, and dealing with it takes hands, and coin is simpler.

When you get back at dusk Martha takes the sack at the kitchen door and opens it to look.

“Hare,” she says. “Three.”

She lifts the sack to weigh it in her hand and opens it a second time.

“And pheasant.”

She does not thank you. She turns and goes into the kitchen, calling for people before she is through the door.

The kitchen light burned very late that night. What the tenants ate at midday the next day was not what they usually eat.
